A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same TRAP benchmark. Their complete main texts, tables, figures and appendices are readable and support reliable matching, including relocated and renumbered material.

before.justification: v1 reports original experiments comprising 3,780 agent runs and 948 successful attacks, alongside controlled interface, location and tailoring studies.

after.justification: v2 retains those original experiments and adds quantitative modality-comparison results, agent-log case analyses and a chaining demonstration.

M1.justification: The five-component injection construction, agent observation-action loop, AXTree default and one-click benchmark criterion remain unchanged. The added chaining illustration does not establish a revised TRAP algorithm or agent architecture.

E1.justification: The six website clones, 18 benign tasks and 630 benchmark combinations are retained. Figure 15 adds a limited GoMail case that continues onto an attacker-controlled verification page, extending demonstrated scenarios beyond the initial redirection.

E2.justification: The six-model comparison and comparator membership in the retained interface, location and tailoring experiments are unchanged. Newly cited research is not added as an experimentally evaluated baseline.

E3.justification: Figure 15 adds a demonstration using an account-balance prompt explicitly permitting verification and follows agent actions after redirection. The main benchmark retains its metrics, AXTree observations, temperature 0 and 35-step limit. Appendix F newly documents settings for the modality comparison already mentioned in v1.

E4.justification: New Appendix E substantially expands diagnostic analysis through successful hijacks, detection, silent ignoring, seed-dependent outcomes, framing sensitivity and hallucination cases. Appendix F quantifies the previously brief modality comparison, while Appendix C.4 adds a chaining case. The existing interface, location and tailoring analyses remain.

E5.justification: v2 introduces formal uncertainty reporting across all six main ASRs through 95% binomial confidence intervals in Table 1, plus Fisher exact tests in Appendix F. Appendix E.3 explicitly describes different-seed outcomes. The full-dataset single run and three-run check on 120 tasks remain unchanged; additional benchmark reruns are not established.

E6.justification: The retained numerical results match, including Tables 1–6 and v1 Table 14, now v2 Table 15. New Table 14 reports Gemini/GoCalendar ASRs of 8.7% versus 10.5% and benign utilities of 12.5% versus 8.6% for AXTree versus AXTree plus screenshots. New cases report qualitative failure and resistance outcomes.

T1.justification: Neither version presents substantive theoretical results or proofs. The expanded security-boundary explanation is conceptual, and the statistical additions do not introduce a new formal theory or revise mathematical reasoning.

C1.justification: The contribution statement corrects '630 distinct injections' to '630 task–injection combinations,' aligning it with the existing 18-task × 35-template construction. The headline vulnerability findings and modular-framework contributions otherwise retain their meaning.

C2.justification: v2 adds the limitation that modular decomposition may miss naturally co-occurring persuasion effects, tentative interpretations of agent traces, and a fuller rationale for AXTree and separating initial susceptibility from downstream behavior. These qualify and explain the retained findings.

D1.justification: Appendix F newly specifies the modality comparison's model, environment and sample sizes of 104 and 105; the added cases disclose concrete prompts and action traces. Both versions defer code release. v2 drops the earlier specific promise of staged injection-database release from the relocated ethics statement.

R1.justification: v2 adds Foerster et al. and Rehberger, distinguishes interaction-boundary redirection from prior perception-generation attacks, and strengthens the chaining motivation. It also replaces Cialdini's 2001 article with the 2021 book. These are focused additions to otherwise retained positioning.

P1.justification: v2 polishes paragraphs and headings, removes the duplicated LLaMA location-study paragraph, moves ethics into an Impact Statement, adds acknowledgements and reorganizes appendix material. The main narrative and section sequence remain largely intact.

P2.justification: The main text and references change from predominantly single-column to two-column layout, with extensive resizing and repositioning of displays. Table 3 is reorganized, the targeted/non-targeted prompt figures move to the appendix, and new Figure 15 and modality Table 14 are added.

improvement.justification: Confidence intervals, explicit modality results, behavioral cases and the new applicability limitation improve support and clarity for the unchanged core findings. The gains remain bounded by curated examples and a one-model, one-site ablation. A new reporting flaw partly offsets them: Table 14 claims p > 0.5 for both outcomes, but its utility counts give a standard two-sided Fisher p-value of about 0.38; the non-significance conclusion nevertheless remains valid.
